History and Physical (Detailed)

Consult Summary:
- 40-year-old postpartum woman with sudden onset dyspnea and self-recorded tachycardia 4 weeks after Caesarean section; clinician advised immediate hospital evaluation for possible pulmonary embolism.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Acute shortness of breath that began suddenly ~1 hour before call while sitting watching TV.
- Timeline:
  • Yesterday – developed a dry cough.  
  • 1 hour ago – new dyspnea at rest; aware of rapid heartbeat.  
  • No previous similar episodes.
- Character/associations:
  • Feels “out of breath”; palpitations.  
  • Mild, diffuse chest soreness on deep inspiration; C-section scar also tender.  
  • Denies frank chest pain at rest, hemoptysis, leg pain/swelling, fever.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Stress seems to heighten symptoms; no specific relief measures tried.
- Review of systems (limited to conversation):
  • No upper-respiratory congestion in patient or baby.  
  • No syncope, dizziness, or calf pain discussed.

Past Medical History:
- Caesarean section 4 weeks ago; postoperative recovery otherwise uncomplicated.
- No chronic illnesses reported.

Medications:
- Codeine (post-operative analgesia), last taken ≈1 week ago – dose/route/frequency not documented.
Allergies:
- Ibuprofen – reaction unspecified.

Social History:
- Lives at home with 4-week-old infant; partner currently at work.
- Smoking, alcohol, and other substance use: not discussed.

Family History:
- Mother with history of leg clots (DVT).

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Only pulse assessed remotely. Patient counted 30 beats during timed interval (duration unspecified); clinician interpreted as “slightly fast/tachycardic.” No BP, RR, O₂ saturation, or temperature recorded.
- General, respiratory, cardiovascular, abdominal, extremity exams: Not recorded.

Investigations:
- None performed during tele-consult.

Assessment & Plan:
Overall Impression:
- Sudden dyspnea with tachycardia 4 weeks postpartum is highly suspicious for pulmonary embolism; differential also includes acute respiratory infection and anxiety, but organic causes prioritized.

DDx Integration (concise):
1. Pulmonary embolism (high likelihood) – postpartum hypercoagulability + recent surgery + sudden SOB/tachycardia; pleuritic discomfort supports; no leg symptoms but absence does not exclude.
2. Acute respiratory infection (medium) – new cough; pleuritic soreness; however onset of dyspnea abrupt and afebrile.
3. Anxiety/panic (medium) – patient reports stress/palpitations; objective risk factors favor PE over primary anxiety.

Issue 1: Acute shortness of breath, ?Pulmonary embolism
- Plan:
  • Immediate hospital evaluation advised; patient to self-transport promptly with infant; instructed to bring necessary supplies.  
  • Option of ambulance discussed; patient declined.  
  • ED work-up anticipated: vitals, ECG, D-dimer, CT pulmonary angiography/VQ scan, CXR, baseline labs; anticoagulation per ED findings.  
  • Advised not to take further codeine until evaluated.  
  • Safety-net: call emergency services if symptoms worsen, chest pain develops, or unable to travel.

Issue 2: Recent cough ± respiratory infection
- Plan:
  • Assessment in ED for infectious etiology; manage per findings (e.g., CXR, PCR, antibiotics if indicated).

Issue 3: Post-operative pain management/postpartum care
- Plan:
  • Review postoperative analgesia in hospital; alternative pain control if codeine withheld.  
  • Routine postpartum follow-up unchanged.

General plan items:
- Encourage mobilization when safe to reduce VTE risk in future.  
- Re-address allergy specifics and full medication list at next visit.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: full vital signs (BP, RR, O₂ sat, temp), complete medication reconciliation, detailed allergy reaction.  
● Conflict: DOB stated 20 Apr 1980 by patient; clinician repeated 1983 – conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; physical-exam limited by telehealth context.
